rv.q: The play's central dramatic engine — the collision between Darren's candor and the team's ingrained homophobia — still purrs with relevance and power.
Despite some new tweaks, Greenberg's ambitious script still has a pile-on of themes, dealing with gender, race, sexuality, celebrity and spirituality, not to mention major league sports.
Suavely performed, this new production doesn’t add all that much substance to the conversation.
Take Me Out impresses again with its wit, wisdom, and lyrical appreciation of baseball.
In mapping the existential gap between player and team, between person and tribe, Take Me Out was ahead of its time — and still is.
Nonetheless, “Take Me Out” proves to be the highlight of the current theatrical season, thanks to Greenberg, Ellis and a uniformly superb cast who consistently hit it out of the proverbial park.
